diagnostic_evidence.quote: This transformation preserves the sufficient regularity of the integrand and hence improves the rate of convergence of RQMC.
the author proved that the error rate of $\mathcal{O}(N^{-1+ \epsilon_r})$ can be retained under specific "QMC-friendly" growth conditions on the integrand and its derivatives
and the function $h^{GBM}_1(u_j)$ determines the growth of the integrand at the boundary of $[0,1]$

issues.failure_explanation: The derived 'boundary growth conditions' only make the leading-order ratio of characteristic function to proposal density bounded (or vanishing) as u_j->0. The cited rate result requires growth conditions on the integrand's mixed partial derivatives, plus corner avoidance. The paper never checks derivative growth and never connects its conditions to any rate theorem, yet it states that the conditions 'ensure' nearly optimal rates. Only numerical evidence is provided.

failure_location.quote: Then, we tune the parameters of the proposal density to satisfy the derived boundary growth conditions that ensure nearly optimal convergence rates.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either verify the mixed-derivative growth conditions for the transformed integrands (a contained new analysis per model) or restate the conditions as heuristics ensuring boundedness, backed by numerical evidence.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical convergence-rate guarantee advertised for the proposed transformations (Tables 3-4) is unsupported. Only empirical rates remain.
issues.title: Boundedness conditions are claimed to ensure nearly optimal RQMC rates without any rate analysis
issues.why_classification: The method and numerics survive. However, the claimed guarantee needs either a new nontrivial derivative analysis or a weakening to a heuristic.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper defines hat P(z)=∫e^{iz'x}P and damping e^{-<R,x>}P. Then hat P(y+iR) and Phi(y+iR) both carry e^{iy'x}, and Plancherel gives ∫Pf=(2π)^{-d}∫hat P(y+iR)Phi(-y-iR)dy, not the stated product. In addition, for the basket put with R_j>0 (Table's δ_P, and the positive optimal R_j used), e^{-R'x}P is not integrable as x_j→-∞. The formula and Table 6 match the opposite convention, hat P(z)=∫e^{-iz'x}P with damping e^{<R,x>}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Adopt one convention consistently: hat P(z)=∫e^{-iz'x}P(x)dx and damping e^{<R,x>}P in Assumption 2.1 and in the L^∞ bound argument.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the valuation formula and the strips δ_P are mutually inconsistent, so the integrand g is ill-specified under the paper's own definitions.
issues.title: Fourier convention and damping sign inconsistent with valuation formula and payoff table
issues.why_classification: A consistent sign convention restores everything, with no change to the method or results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $-1\le \rho_{i, j} \le 1$ denotes the correlation between $W_i$ and $W_j$

issues.failure_explanation: The eigenvalues λ_j are those of Σ, and their positivity cannot follow from positive definiteness of the proposal matrix Σ̃; the argument is circular. The model allows |ρ|=1, in which case Σ is only semidefinite, some λ_j=0, and the prescribed Σ̃=Σ^{-1}/T is undefined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume Σ≻0 (e.g., |ρ_ij|<1 with nonsingular correlation) and justify λ_j>0 from it.
issues.overall_effect: The multivariate GBM transformation rule is undefined for degenerate correlation matrices allowed by the model.
issues.title: Positivity of eigenvalues of Σ wrongly justified; Σ^{-1} may not exist under allowed correlations
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard nondegeneracy hypothesis fixes it without changing the method or its scope in practice.

issues.failure_explanation: Per eq:vg_conditions, any ν̃ > 2T/ν − 1 makes h_1^{VG} unbounded. The summary recommendation ν̃ = ν̄ + ε with ε>0 is therefore exactly the singular case. The correct rule (as in Table 3 and the multivariate case) is ν̃ = ν̄ − ε.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the rule by ν̃ = ν̄ − ε, ε ≥ 0 (with ν̃ > 0).
issues.overall_effect: The stated univariate VG transformation rule, followed literally, produces boundary singularities.
issues.title: Recommended VG degrees of freedom ν̃ = ν̄ + ε violates the derived boundary condition
issues.why_classification: A local sign correction consistent with the paper's own derivation and table restores the rule.

issues.failure_explanation: With (ν̃+d)/2 = T/ν, eq:r_VG_multivariate gives h_1 ∝ ((y'Σ̃^{-1}y)/(y'Σy))^{T/ν}. This is a ratio of two positive-definite quadratic forms, homogeneous of degree 0, so it stays between positive constants as |y|→∞ for every Σ̃≻0. It neither diverges when Σ−Σ̃^{-1}≺0 nor tends to 0 when Σ−Σ̃^{-1}≻0. The logarithm-difference sign argument conflates the sign of the exponent with its growth.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the trichotomy by the correct statement: for ν̃=2T/ν−d the ratio is bounded for every Σ̃≻0, with limit constant ∝ sqrt(det Σ̃)·λ_max(Σ^{-1/2}Σ̃^{-1}Σ^{-1/2})^{T/ν}. Then re-justify the choice of Σ̃ by minimizing that constant.
issues.overall_effect: The boundary growth condition Σ−Σ̃^{-1}⪰0 listed in Table 4 for ν̃=2T/ν−d is misderived (unnecessary). The rationale for selecting Σ̃ is incorrect.
issues.title: False trichotomy for multivariate VG with ν̃ = 2T/ν − d (ratio is degree-0 homogeneous)
issues.why_classification: Boundedness under the recommended choices survives, but the advertised condition and the selection criterion must be re-derived.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the boundary growth of $r^{NIG}(\boldsymbol{u})$ is controlled by the following term:
Consequently, we constructed the matrix $\boldsymbol{\tilde{\Sigma}}$ by setting

issues.failure_explanation: eq:T_NIG drops the polynomial prefactors (q/2)^{v/2}(2√(2q))^{-1/2} of the Laplace density asymptotics (eq:lap_pdf_as_exp), with q=y'Σ̃^{-1}y and v=(2−d)/2. Hence 1/ψ_lap ∝ q^{(d−1)/4}e^{√(2q)}. The NIG characteristic function has no compensating polynomial factor. In case (ii) the exponentials cancel and |r^{NIG}| ~ C q^{(d−1)/4} → ∞ for d≥2, not √det Σ̃. The adopted minimal-determinant construction is exactly this critical case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the polynomial factors in the analysis and require strict case (iii), e.g. Σ̃ = c·2Δ^{-1}/(δT)^2 with c>1 (exponential decay dominates). Alternatively, prove boundedness using the payoff-transform decay. Update Table 4 and the parameter choices.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed boundedness of the recommended multivariate NIG transformation (Table 4 with equality, used in the experiments) fails for d≥2. Boundedness then relies on decay of the payoff transform.
issues.title: Multivariate NIG critical choice Σ̃ = 2Δ^{-1}/(δT)^2 leaves polynomially growing ratio for d ≥ 2
issues.why_classification: A contained re-derivation and a modified parameter rule restore bounded ratios, but the stated optimal construction and its claimed limit must be changed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For the TP approach, only central processing unit (CPU) times of up to six dimensions are measured in Python, and the values for the remaining dimensions are numerically extrapolated.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper repeatedly claims that the experiments demonstrate gains for up to 15 assets, but the stated set of tested dimensions stops at d=10. The TP costs beyond d=6 are extrapolated rather than measured, so outperformance of TP beyond d=6 is not established by computation.

failure_location.quote: the RQMC method significantly outperforms the MC method and TP quadrature for options with up to 15 underlying assets for the GBM, VG, and NIG models.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the dimensions actually tested consistently, and qualify comparisons beyond d=6 as being against extrapolated TP costs (or measure them).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised empirical scope (up to 15 assets, especially versus TP) exceeds what the described experiments support.
issues.title: Claimed superiority up to 15 assets not matched by stated tested dimensions and extrapolated TP costs
issues.why_classification: Rewording the scope, or adding the stated runs, fixes it without affecting the method or the analysis.
